name: HARROW CIRCUIT: Shelf Obstacle Endurance League
description: The Harrow Circuit is a semi-legal endurance obstacle competition run through live sections of the Shelf's derelict infrastructure — flooded sub-basements, unstable elevated walkways, live electrical hazards, and active industrial zones — with courses that change every season based on what sections of the Shelf have newly collapsed or been abandoned. No augmentation limits are enforced, but the impoverished athlete base means most competitors run clean or with basic functional chrome. The circuit is governed loosely by the Shelf Athletic Compact, a community organization with no legal standing.
story_hooks: A city infrastructure inspector who signed off on a section of the Harrow Circuit course as 'stable' — knowing it wasn't — is now watching the race from a rooftop, waiting to see if her decision kills anyone.

A Tier 3 documentary filmmaker arrives to make what she expects to be a poverty-tourism piece and instead becomes entangled with a circuit organizer who is being pressured by a local crime syndicate to redirect betting revenue.

An athlete who has won the Harrow Circuit three years running is approached by an APEX IRON scout — and must decide whether the corporate contract that promises chrome, money, and safety is worth the loss of everything the circuit means to her.
